<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<bpmn:definitions xmlns:bpmn="http://www.omg.org/spec/BPMN/20100524/MODEL"
                  id="Definitions_LegoMachine"
                  targetNamespace="http://example.com/bpmn/lego-machine">
  <bpmn:process id="Process_LegoMachine" name="Building a custom machine out of Lego bricks" isExecutable="false">

    <bpmn:startEvent id="StartEvent_Begin" name="Start building"/>

    <bpmn:task id="Task_DevelopDesign" name="Develop basic design"/>

    <bpmn:task id="Task_OrderSets" name="Order Lego brick sets"/>

    <bpmn:manualTask id="Task_SortParts" name="Children sort parts into containers"/>

    <bpmn:exclusiveGateway id="Gateway_Parts_Join" name="Parts join"/>

    <bpmn:exclusiveGateway id="Gateway_Parts_Available" name="Container has parts?" default="Flow_PartsEmpty"/>

    <bpmn:task id="Task_ReorderParts" name="Reorder individual parts"/>

    <bpmn:task id="Task_BuildSubcomponent" name="Build subcomponent"/>

    <bpmn:task id="Task_TestSubcomponent" name="Test subcomponent individually"/>

    <bpmn:exclusiveGateway id="Gateway_Test_Result" name="Test successful?" default="Flow_TestFailed"/>

    <bpmn:task id="Task_RedesignSubcomponent" name="Redesign subcomponent"/>

    <bpmn:task id="Task_RebuildSubcomponent" name="Rebuild subcomponent"/>

    <bpmn:task id="Task_AssembleSubcomponents" name="Assemble subcomponents"/>

    <bpmn:endEvent id="EndEvent_Machine" name="Machine assembled"/>

    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_Start" sourceRef="StartEvent_Begin" targetRef="Task_DevelopDesign"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_DesignDone" sourceRef="Task_DevelopDesign" targetRef="Task_OrderSets"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_SetsOrdered" sourceRef="Task_OrderSets" targetRef="Task_SortParts"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_PartsSorted" sourceRef="Task_SortParts" targetRef="Gateway_Parts_Join"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_Reordered" sourceRef="Task_ReorderParts" targetRef="Gateway_Parts_Join"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_CheckParts" sourceRef="Gateway_Parts_Join" targetRef="Gateway_Parts_Available"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_PartsAvailable" name="Yes" sourceRef="Gateway_Parts_Available" targetRef="Task_BuildSubcomponent">
      <bpmn:conditionExpression xsi:type="bpmn:tFormalExpression" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">${containerHasParts}</bpmn:conditionExpression>
    </bpmn:sequenceFlow>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_PartsEmpty" name="No" sourceRef="Gateway_Parts_Available" targetRef="Task_ReorderParts"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_Built" sourceRef="Task_BuildSubcomponent" targetRef="Task_TestSubcomponent"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_Tested" sourceRef="Task_TestSubcomponent" targetRef="Gateway_Test_Result"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_TestPassed" name="Yes" sourceRef="Gateway_Test_Result" targetRef="Task_AssembleSubcomponents">
      <bpmn:conditionExpression xsi:type="bpmn:tFormalExpression" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">${testSuccessful}</bpmn:conditionExpression>
    </bpmn:sequenceFlow>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_TestFailed" name="No" sourceRef="Gateway_Test_Result" targetRef="Task_RedesignSubcomponent"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_Redesigned" sourceRef="Task_RedesignSubcomponent" targetRef="Task_RebuildSubcomponent"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_Rebuilt" sourceRef="Task_RebuildSubcomponent" targetRef="Task_TestSubcomponent"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_Assembled" sourceRef="Task_AssembleSubcomponents" targetRef="EndEvent_Machine"/>

  </bpmn:process>
</bpmn:definitions>

rules.instruction: When the description states that several items are each checked after their own build step, and that a following joint step on all of the items is performed only when every check succeeds, while a failed check leads to rework of that item: Model each check as its own task on its item, placed after that item's build step. After the checks, place an exclusive gateway with a question about whether all checks succeeded. Give one outgoing sequence flow to the joint step and one to the rework path. Do not omit this gateway, and do not connect the checks straight to the joint step. If the rework is followed by the checks again, route it back through an exclusive merge.
rules.situation: the description states that several items are each checked after their own build step, and that a following joint step on all of the items is performed only when every check succeeds, while a failed check leads to rework of that item

rules.instruction: When the description states that a later step is performed only if a condition on the outcomes of earlier work holds, either for every item in a set (for example, all items must succeed before the next step) or while a supply of items still remains, and it states a different corrective action for the case where the condition fails: Model the condition as an exclusive gateway placed after the activity or activities that produce the outcomes it checks, and before the gated step. Give the branch where the condition holds a labeled outgoing flow to the gated step. Give the failing branch a labeled outgoing flow to the stated corrective task. If the description says the work resumes or is checked again afterwards, route the corrective task's outgoing flow back into a merge gateway placed before this gateway. Do not omit the decision point, and do not connect the corrective task directly to the gated step.
rules.situation: the description states that a later step is performed only if a condition on the outcomes of earlier work holds, either for every item in a set (for example, all items must succeed before the next step) or while a supply of items still remains, and it states a different corrective action for the case where the condition fails

rules.instruction: When the description states that items acquired by an earlier step are handed over to a group of people, who then carry out a sorting or processing activity on those items, so the handover is a separate step between the acquisition and the group's work: Model the handover as its own manual task performed by the person who hands the items over. Place it after the task that acquires the items and before the group's sorting or processing task, with sequence flows connecting them in that order. Do not omit the handover and do not merge it into the group's task.
rules.situation: the description states that items acquired by an earlier step are handed over to a group of people, who then carry out a sorting or processing activity on those items, so the handover is a separate step between the acquisition and the group's work

rules.instruction: When the description states that a repeated activity draws its inputs from a supply that can run out, and that when the supply is exhausted a replenishment action must happen before the activity can continue: Model an exclusive gateway directly after each use of the supply by the repeated activity, asking whether the supply still has items. Give the branch where items remain a condition matching that wording and route it onward to the next step. Give the exhausted branch a condition matching the empty state and route it to the replenishment activity the description names, then return the flow to the point where the supply is used. Do not place the check only before the first use, and do not leave the exhausted outcome without a continuation.
rules.situation: the description states that a repeated activity draws its inputs from a supply that can run out, and that when the supply is exhausted a replenishment action must happen before the activity can continue

rules.instruction: When the description states that a follow-up activity is performed only if a stated condition on a state or item holds (an 'if ... then ...' clause, such as a resource being exhausted or a check not being passed), and otherwise the process continues its normal flow: Model an exclusive gateway placed before the conditional activity, labeled with the condition as a question. One outgoing flow leads to the conditional activity, and a second flow bypasses it to the normal next step. Close both paths with an exclusive gateway before the process continues. Do not connect the conditional activity as an unconditional step in the main sequence, and do not omit the gateway that makes the condition explicit.
rules.situation: the description states that a follow-up activity is performed only if a stated condition on a state or item holds (an 'if ... then ...' clause, such as a resource being exhausted or a check not being passed), and otherwise the process continues its normal flow

rules.instruction: When the description states that a later step is performed only if a stated condition holds, using an 'if ... then' phrasing that gates that step on a decision made earlier in the process: Model an exclusive gateway immediately before the gated step, with one outgoing branch that leads to the gated step under the stated condition and another branch that skips it or leads to the process's alternative path. Keep the gateway after the activity that establishes the condition, so the decision is evaluated in the order the description gives.
rules.situation: the description states that a check or verification follows an earlier activity, and that a later activity is carried out only if the check succeeds, while a failed check leads to a rework activity

promoted.trigger: the description says that something obtained in an earlier step is passed on to a set of performers who then process it, so the passing-on is a distinct step between obtaining it and the performers' processing
promoted.instruction: Model the passing-on as its own manual task performed by the party that passes it on. Place it after the task that obtains the object and before the performers' processing task, connected by sequence flows in that order. Do not omit the passing-on step and do not merge it into the processing task.
promoted.detail: general form of EXS-066, written after it improved the model of example 34

promoted.trigger: the description states that a repeated activity consumes an input that can be exhausted, and that once the input is exhausted a named replenishment step must occur before the activity can proceed
promoted.instruction: Model an exclusive gateway directly after each consumption of the input by the repeated activity, with a condition asking whether the input remains. Assign the branch where input remains a condition matching that wording and route it onward to the next step. Assign the exhausted branch a condition matching the empty state and route it to the replenishment step the description names, then return the flow to the point of consumption. Do not place the check only before the first consumption, and do not leave the exhausted outcome without a continuation.
